title: API Holdings Clears All Debt, Releases Thyrocare Share Pledge in PharmEasy Turnaround
excerpt: PharmEasy's parent repays ₹1,050 crore through Thyrocare stake sale and internal accruals, removing all encumbrances from promoter holding
body:
• API Holdings, PharmEasy's parent company, has become debt-free after repaying its outstanding ₹1,050 crore (~$125 million) obligation
  • Docon Technologies retains a 51.02% controlling stake in listed diagnostics firm Thyrocare, now fully unencumbered
  • The debt clearance marks the end of a ₹2,700 crore borrowing cycle that began with the 2021 Thyrocare acquisition
  • Thyrocare shares trade near 52-week highs at ~₹620, up 35% over the past year, with FY26 profit rising 81%

Debt Cleared Through Asset Sales and Cash Flow

API Holdings, the parent company of India's largest online pharmacy PharmEasy and listed diagnostics firm Thyrocare Technologies, announced on August 17 that it has become entirely debt-free. The company repaid its remaining ₹1,050 crore (~$125 million) in outstanding debt using proceeds from a partial sale of its stake in Thyrocare and internal accruals.

The repayment triggered the release of all pledged Thyrocare shares held by Docon Technologies, the API Holdings subsidiary that serves as Thyrocare's promoter entity. Docon now holds a 51.02% controlling stake in Thyrocare, down from 71.06% before successive stake sales, but entirely free of encumbrances for the first time since API Holdings acquired Thyrocare in 2021.

End of a Prolonged Debt Cycle

The debt-free milestone caps a turbulent four-year financial saga. API Holdings originally borrowed roughly ₹2,200 crore from Kotak Mahindra Bank to fund its 2021 acquisition of Thyrocare at a time when the health-tech startup was valued at $5.6 billion. That loan was refinanced in May 2022 through a ₹2,700 crore facility from Goldman Sachs, carrying interest rates of 17-18% annually.

By mid-2023, PharmEasy had breached restrictive covenants on the Goldman Sachs debt, though it continued meeting repayment schedules. A ₹2,400 crore rights issue — executed at a 90% markdown to API Holdings' peak valuation — provided partial relief, with participation from existing shareholders TPG, Temasek, and the Manipal Group's Ranjan Pai.

"API will consider an IPO when it is profitable ex-Thyrocare, as well as debt-free. That is the time when any corporate action will be considered."

— Rahul Guha, Group CEO, API Holdings & MD/CEO, Thyrocare

In September 2025, API Holdings raised ₹1,700 crore through non-convertible debentures led by 360 One (₹1,231 crore), with participation from Micro Labs, Bennett Coleman, and others. Docon pledged 61% of Thyrocare's equity — approximately 3.23 crore shares — as collateral. The proceeds retired ₹1,545.4 crore in prior NCD obligations.

A month later, Docon sold a 10% stake in Thyrocare through a bulk deal for ₹668 crore to institutional buyers including HDFC AMC, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, and Eastspring Investments. That sale brought the debt down from ₹1,800 crore to ₹1,050 crore by mid-2026, setting up the final repayment.

Thyrocare's Profit Surge Underpins the Recovery

Thyrocare's own financial performance has been central to the turnaround. In FY26 (April 2025 – March 2026), the diagnostics company posted revenue growth of 21%, with profit after tax jumping 81% for the full year. Q4 FY26 was particularly strong: revenue rose 20% to ₹223.95 crore and PAT surged 128% to ₹48.7 crore.

The company generated free cash flow of approximately ₹192 crore in FY26 and raised its dividend by 56%. Its partnership (B2B) revenue grew 32%, reflecting deeper integration with hospital chains and lab networks.

On the NSE, Thyrocare shares traded at roughly ₹610-620 on August 18, within striking distance of their 52-week high of ₹662 and well above the 52-week low of ₹343. The stock has gained about 35% over the past year, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately ₹9,700 crore (~$1.15 billion). At a trailing P/E of roughly 55, the stock prices in continued earnings growth.

What Comes Next for API Holdings

The debt clearance removes a major overhang that had weighed on investor sentiment around both Thyrocare and the broader API Holdings group. With PharmEasy's parent now debt-free and Thyrocare's promoter holding unencumbered, the path to a potential API Holdings IPO — long delayed from its original 2023 timeline — becomes more plausible.

API Holdings reported a 14.7% revenue increase to ₹5,095.5 crore for the first nine months of FY26 and posted a positive EBITDA (excluding ESOPs) of ₹29.2 crore, its first such milestone. The B2B distribution segment turned EBITDA-positive in Q3 FY26, and working capital days improved from 50 to 40.

Group CEO Rahul Guha, who also serves as Thyrocare's managing director, told analysts in July 2026 that an IPO was "at least 12 months away," contingent on the core PharmEasy business achieving profitability independent of Thyrocare. With the debt now cleared, the remaining hurdle is operational — turning the e-pharmacy from a loss-maker into a self-sustaining business.

Control of PharmEasy rests largely with institutional investors — Ranjan Pai's family office, Prosus, TPG, and Temasek — following the departure of most cofounders from executive roles. Cofounder Siddharth Shah stepped down as CEO in August 2025; cofounders Dharmil Sheth, Dhaval Shah, and Hardik Dedhia had exited earlier to launch a separate venture.
